data_keys_hint: ↵ edit · Del NULL · Ctrl Del delete row · Ctrl Z undo

data_bad_hex: {column} is binary: type the bytes as hex, \x0a1f or 0x0A1F.
err_transaction_open: A transaction is already open: commit or roll it back first.

plan_running: Asking the server for the plan…
plan_empty: Put the cursor on a query and press Explain.
plan_measured_rolled_back: EXPLAIN ANALYZE · run at {time} in a rolled back transaction
plan_reason_requested: You asked for the planner's estimate only.
plan_reason_production_write: On production a writing statement is never run: this is the estimate only.
plan_reason_no_safe_rollback: MySQL and MariaDB cannot promise to undo a write on every table: estimate only.
plan_reason_no_savepoint: DuckDB has no savepoints: inside an open transaction a write cannot be undone on its own, so estimate only.
plan_reason_engine_cannot_measure: {engine} does not measure time: the plan shows the order of reads.
plan_rolled_back_note: The statement writes: it ran to be measured and was rolled back at once.
plan_unreadable: The plan could not be read: below is the text the server returned.
plan_legend_slow: occupied track: where the time goes
plan_legend_flow: left to right, as the server runs it
plan_section: Section A-A · exclusive time per node
plan_section_cost: Section A-A · exclusive cost per node
plan_summary_measured: The query took {total}. The heaviest step is {op}: {share} of the time.
plan_summary_estimated: The planner expects the heaviest step to be {op}: {share} of the cost.
plan_summary_order: The server reads the tables in this order: {steps}.
plan_none: Nothing to report: the plan uses the right indexes and the estimates are close to reality.
plan_try_note: Try it on a non-production environment first.
plan_compare_hint: Against the previous plan of this tab.
plan_f_seq_scan_body: The server reads all {rows} rows of {table} to keep {kept}. An index on {column} takes it straight to the right rows.
plan_f_seq_scan_body_nocol: The server reads all {rows} rows of {table} to keep {kept}. An index on the filter columns avoids the full read.
plan_f_fk_body: {table}.{column} refers to {ref} but has no index: to join the tables the server reads all {rows} rows of {table} and uses {kept}.
plan_f_estimate_body: The planner expected {est} rows and got {rows}. With estimates like these it can pick the wrong plan.
plan_f_estimate_body_table: The planner expected {est} rows and got {rows}. Refreshing the statistics of {table} helps it choose better.
plan_f_spill_body: It does not fit in working memory and writes {size} to temporary files. More working memory for the session, or fewer rows to handle, keeps it in memory.
plan_f_spill_body_nosize: It does not fit in working memory and goes through temporary files. More working memory for the session, or fewer rows to handle, keeps it in memory.
plan_f_loop_body: The inner side on {table} repeats {loops} times and reads {rows} rows in all. An index on the join column, or a JOIN with GROUP BY, avoids the repetition.
plan_f_function_body: {column} has an index, but the filter wraps it in {fn}(): the server cannot use it and reads all {rows} rows of {table}. Compare the column as it is, or index the expression.
plan_f_cast_body: {table}.{column} is converted to {type} for the comparison, so its index does not help. Compare it with a value of its own type.
plan_f_star_body: The server sorts {rows} rows {width} bytes wide because the query asks for every column of {table}. List only the ones you need and the sort gets lighter.
plan_f_limit_body: The query returns {rows} rows. If you need a few, a LIMIT saves work on the server and memory in the app.

sort_multiple: Not sortable: several statements at once
sort_duplicates: Not sortable: MySQL refuses two columns with the same name
sort_running: Sorting is possible once the query has finished

tool_restore_import_adds: The folder's tables are added to the database; nothing is deleted.
tool_user_mssql_hint: SQL Server: creates a database user without a login (WITHOUT LOGIN). Logins are created at server level, with CREATE LOGIN.
sec_readonly: Read-only: it changes nothing and never tries a password. Fixes are SQL for you to review and run.
sec_idle: Reads the server settings and tells you what is wrong in plain words, with the fix to copy.
sec_summary: {high} high · {medium} medium · {low} low · {passed} passed · {skipped} not checked
sec_fix_note: Review before running. On production it goes through the write gate. Replace any placeholders in angle brackets.
sec_none: No problems found among the checks that could run.
sec_skip_privilege: The connected user cannot read this data
sec_skip_not_detectable: The engine does not record it: not visible from here
sec_list_updated: List updated to {date}: check run again.
sec_list_current: The list of {date} is already the latest.
sec_snapshot: Versions list of {date}. It does not replace the vendor's advisories.
sec_report_head: Report generated by NiceDB, read-only. It does not replace a full security audit.
sec_unsupported: Nothing to check for this engine: there is no server with accounts, network and privileges.
sec_c_superusers_what: A superuser can read and change any data and even switch the safeguards off. If the password leaks, no data is safe. Keep only the accounts that administration really needs.
sec_c_default_accounts_what: Names such as sa, root or postgres are the first ones an attacker tries. If they are enabled and reachable over the network, guessing the password is all it takes. Lock or rename them and administer with a less obvious account.
sec_c_anonymous_accounts_what: There are accounts with no name: anyone can connect without saying who they are. They should be dropped.
sec_c_weak_passwords_what: Some accounts have no password, store it with an old method (md5) or have no strength rules. The check only reads the server catalogs: it never tries to guess a password. A passwordless account can be intended if it signs in with a certificate or the local socket.
sec_c_public_grants_what: A privilege granted to PUBLIC applies to every user on the server, including those created later. On these objects anyone who can connect can read or write.
sec_c_ddl_rights_title: Users who can change the structure
sec_c_ddl_rights_what: An application user should read and write data, not create, alter or drop tables. If its credentials are stolen, or the application has a bug, a single statement can wipe out a whole table.
sec_c_hba_trust_what: pg_hba.conf rules with the trust method let in anyone coming from that address without asking for a password. The password method sends it in clear text. On the local socket the risk is smaller, but it remains.
sec_c_hba_md5_what: md5 is an old method: whoever intercepts the exchange can reuse the password hash. scram-sha-256 is the current method and does not have this flaw. Passwords must be reset after the change.
sec_c_hba_open_what: These rules accept connections from the whole network and do not force encryption. Restrict the addresses to the ones needed and use hostssl.
sec_c_ssl_what: Without TLS passwords and data travel in clear text and anyone in between can read them. Turn encryption on at the server and make it mandatory.
sec_c_listen_all_what: The server accepts connections on every network card. If that is not needed, limit it to the internal address or localhost and put a firewall in front.
sec_c_server_version_what: The server version appears in a list of known vulnerabilities, or its support has ended and it gets no more fixes. Upgrade to the version shown within the same series.
sec_c_sensitive_columns_what: Columns that by name or content look like tax codes, IBANs, emails or phone numbers, with no encryption or row-level security. To recognise them the check reads at most five values per column: it keeps and shows none of them.
sec_c_logging_what: Without connection and error logs you cannot tell who connected, nor notice sign-in attempts.
sec_c_backup_recent_what: No full backup shows up in the last 7 days. A backup that does not exist is the worst problem exactly when you need it.
sec_c_risky_features_what: Extensions and options that let the server run commands, read files or talk to other servers. Turn off the ones you do not use.

panel_scripts_empty: The scripts you save show up here, ready to open, insert or run.

settings_row_cap_hint: Past the cap reading stops and the result is marked as truncated.
settings_display_hint: Only changes how cells look: copy, export and editing use the real value.
settings_timeout_hint: A query that runs past the limit is cancelled on the server.
settings_unlock_hint: Only for timed unlocking: when the time is up writes lock again by themselves.
settings_keys_hint: Click a shortcut and press the new keys. If they are taken, the old ones stay.
key_needs_modifier: Use at least one modifier such as Ctrl, Alt or Shift.
guard_hint_typed: Every write still asks for the connection name.
guard_hint_modal: Every write still asks for a confirmation.
settings_unlock_mode_hint: How writing opens on production connections. The production stamp stays visible either way.
settings_unlock_timed_hint: You unlock for the time chosen below, then the connection goes back to read-only by itself.
settings_unlock_session_hint: You unlock once and writes stay open until you close the connection, with no countdown.
settings_unlock_open_hint: Production is never read-only and there is nothing to unlock: the least protected choice.
settings_confirm_mode_hint: Also governs the risky-statement warning (UPDATE or DELETE without WHERE, DROP, TRUNCATE). The write log always records every write.
settings_confirm_typed_hint: Each write needs the connection name typed: the strongest guard against the wrong connection.
settings_confirm_modal_hint: A dialog with Cancel and Confirm appears, nothing to type; focus starts on Cancel.
settings_confirm_none_hint: Writes go straight through, even UPDATE and DELETE without WHERE: only the log remembers them.
resize_panel: Notes, scripts and snippets panel width
tool_rows_hint: Rows of two queries or tables
rows_lead: Compare the rows of two queries or tables by key and write the script that brings the target in line with the source.
rows_source_hint: The rows as they should be, for example staging.
rows_target_hint: The rows to bring in line, for example production.
rows_key_hint: The columns that identify a row on both sides.
rows_key_none: Pick at least one column the two sides share.
rows_key_wait: The columns show up once both sources can be read.
rows_added_hint: Only in the source: the script inserts them.
rows_removed_hint: Only in the target: the script deletes them.
rows_changed_hint: Same key, different values: the script updates them.
rows_same_hint: Equal on both sides, usually hidden.
rows_read: {target} rows in the target, {source} in the source, in {time}.
rows_same_cut: Only the first {count} equal rows are shown.
rows_equal: The two sources have the same rows.
rows_none_shown: No rows match the chosen filters.
rows_cancelled: Comparison cancelled: the differences are partial and no script is written.
rows_idle: Pick the two sources and the key, then compare.
rows_script_hint: {count} statements for {engine}, to review: nothing runs by itself.
rows_script_big: The script has {count} statements: better to save it as a file than to open it in the editor.
rows_script_cols: Columns found on one side only are left out of the script.
rows_fault_key_missing: Column {column} is not in both sources.
rows_fault_duplicate: The key is not unique: the {side} has more than one row with {key}. Pick columns that identify a single row.
rows_fault_too_large: The comparison went past {limit} MB of memory after {rows} rows. Sort both queries by the key or narrow them with a WHERE.
session_init_hint: They run every time a session opens: after a reconnect, on a database switch and in the side connections of tools and import. If one fails, the session does not open.
session_keepalive_hint: A SELECT 1 on an idle session, never while a query runs.
session_row_limit_hint: For SELECTs without LIMIT, TOP or FETCH. Empty: the cap in Settings applies ({count}).
session_row_limit_bad: Enter a number from 1 to 2,000,000, or leave it empty.
session_reconnect: Reconnect on its own when the connection drops
session_reconnect_hint: Same profile, tunnel and password, then the init queries again. An interrupted query is never run again.
session_dropped_restored: The connection dropped during statement {index} and was restored.
session_dropped_lost: The connection dropped during statement {index} and cannot be restored.
session_dropped_write: It was a write: it may have run. Check the data before running it again.
session_dropped_read: It was a read: running it again is safe.
session_tx_lost: The server rolled back the open transaction.
session_restored_tx: {name}: connection restored, the open transaction was rolled back.
session_idle_closed: {name}: closed after being idle. It opens again on next use.
results_limited: Connection limit: showing the first {count} rows.
wizard_language_hint: It applies to menus, messages and warnings. The text changes at once.
wizard_look_hint: Style, palette and theme change the whole app at once.
wizard_comfort_hint: Fit the interface to your screen. The editor font can stay as it is.
wizard_safety_hint: The careful options are already chosen: production opens for writing only for a few minutes, and every write asks for the connection's name.
wizard_ready_hint: These are your choices. You can change them any time in Settings.
wizard_skip_body: Anything you haven't chosen yet stays as it is. You can reopen the setup from Settings.
wizard_unlock_timed_hint: You unlock for {count} minutes, then the connection goes back to read-only on its own. The length can be changed in Settings.
fk_rows_unknown: Count too slow, stopped after 2 seconds
fk_none_out: This table has no foreign keys.
fk_none_in: No table points to this one.
fk_no_row: Pick a row to see where it leads and what refers to it.
fk_picker_slow: No rows found within 3 seconds: the table is large and has no suitable index. Type something more precise, such as the key.
tx_mode_manual_hint: Everything waits for Commit or Rollback.
tx_mode_smart_hint: Automatic while you read; from the first write it waits for Commit.
tx_commit_note: The dry run's writes become permanent.
tx_commit_locked: Unlock writes to commit on production.
tx_implicit: MySQL committed the open transaction before statement {index}: DDL statements commit by themselves.
tx_lost_before: The connection had dropped: the open transaction is gone, with its writes.
tx_err_failed: The transaction failed: it can only be rolled back.
tx_err_not_dry: Statement {index} cannot run as a dry run: {sql}
tx_dry_hint: Runs inside a transaction, shows the rows it touches and waits for Commit or Rollback
tx_dry_banner: Dry run: {summary}. Nothing is kept until you press Commit.
tx_dry_failed: The dry run stopped on an error and was rolled back.
tx_dry_committed: Dry run committed: the changes are written.
tx_dry_rolled_back: Dry run rolled back: nothing was kept.
tx_dry_estimate: New values estimated before running: this engine or table cannot rehearse the UPDATE and roll it back, so now(), triggers and defaults may write something else.
tx_dry_no_preview: For this statement the engine gives only the count, not the rows.
tx_dry_empty: No write statement in this dry run.
tx_close_space_title: Switch space with an open transaction?
tx_close_body: Closing the connection makes the server roll back everything not committed.
data_applied_held_one: 1 change in the transaction: commit it to keep it.
data_applied_held_other: {count} changes in the transaction: commit them to keep them.
session_idle_closed_tx: {name}: closed after being idle. The open transaction was rolled back.
pal_hint_objects: Tables, views, columns and functions of open connections
pal_hint_library: Scripts, bookmarks, notes, snippets, connections and workspaces
pal_hint_commands: What do you want to do?
pal_objects_closed: No open connection. Objects come from the schema of open connections: open one from Library.
pal_find_session: session process kill terminate cancel sessione
pal_button_hint: Search everywhere: objects, library and commands
pal_button_hint_keys: Search everywhere: objects, library and commands ({keys})
mon_slow_none: No statistics for this database yet.
mon_explain_hint: Opens the query in a tab and draws its estimated plan, without running it
mon_explain_none: Plans are not available for this engine yet
mon_explain_params: The query has placeholders where the constants were: type the values in the parameters bar, then press Explain.
mon_plan_cache_note: Meanwhile the queries come from the plan cache, which empties at every restart.
mon_gap_file: It is a file: there is no server with sessions and connections to count.
mon_gap_not_exposed: This engine does not expose it.
mon_gap_permission: This user cannot read it: it needs {need}.
mon_gap_ext_missing: The {name} extension is not installed in this database.
mon_gap_ext_not_loaded: The {name} extension is installed, but the server does not load it.
mon_howto_pgss: Turn it on with CREATE EXTENSION pg_stat_statements; the server must have it in shared_preload_libraries, which takes a restart.
mon_howto_pgss_preload: Add pg_stat_statements to shared_preload_libraries in postgresql.conf and restart the server.
mon_howto_perfschema: Turn it on with performance_schema = ON in the server configuration, then restart.
mon_howto_querystore: Turn it on with ALTER DATABASE … SET QUERY_STORE = ON.
mon_maintain_note: Runs on a connection of its own. On large tables it can take long and slow others down.
mon_file_note: It is a file with no server: no sessions, locks, cache or query statistics to show. Here is the space it takes; VACUUM and ANALYZE are in the menu of the database and its tables.
vp_cmd_record: Show the row as a record
vp_no_cell: Pick a cell in the grid.
vp_record_keys: ↑ ↓ change row · Tab next field · Enter opens the value
vp_row_deleted: The row is marked for deletion.
vp_bin_edit: Change a binary value by loading a file or editing its bytes as hex: it stays pending until Apply.
vp_image_broken: The preview does not open: the bytes are not a complete image.
params_raw_warning: SQL name: written into the text as is. Table or column names only.
params_asked: Give the new parameters a value, then press Enter.
params_err_invalid: The value of {name} is not a valid {kind}.
params_err_raw: {name} takes only a table or column name, with no spaces or quotes.
search_lead: Look for a text or a number in every table, one at a time and read-only.
search_case_hint: Tells upper case from lower case
search_kind_number_off: The value is not a number
search_tables_placeholder: all, or parts of the name
search_views_hint: Slower: a view is computed again for each search and has no statistics for the estimate.
search_stopped: The search stopped when you switched view: below are the tables already searched.
search_estimate_none: No suitable column: change the column types or the tables.
search_prod: Production: the queries only read, but on large tables they read everything.
search_heavy_note: The queries only read, but large tables without a fitting index are read in full and load the server. The search stops after {time} anyway.
search_nothing: No row holds “{value}” in the tables searched.
search_out_of_time: Out of time: {count} tables not searched. Raise the time limit or narrow the tables.
search_open_hint: Opens the row in the Data view, in a new tab
search_no_key: No key: the row opens filtered on the column found.
search_idle: Type a value and press Enter. The columns searched depend on the value: a number is also looked for in numeric columns, a date or a code in columns of other types.
search_no_schema: The schema is not loaded yet.
cmp_continue_on_error: In scripts, continue after an error
cmp_stop_on_error: In scripts, stop at the first error
cmp_inspections_off: Stop underlining unknown tables and columns
cmp_kind_alias: Alias or table of the query
cmp_unknown_note: According to the loaded schema. It does not stop the run.
model_is_hint: A template is never opened: it is for creating similar connections. When you change it, the change reaches the connections that follow it, except the fields they made their own.
model_no_followers: No connection follows it yet: create the first from the template's menu.
model_follows_hint: Fields equal to the template keep following it. Fields you change here become this connection's own.
model_own_title: Own field: changes to the template leave it alone
model_open_hint: A template: edit it, it does not open
err_model: A template does not open: open a connection that follows it.
err_no_keyring: No default keyring to keep the password in. Create one in Seahorse (GNOME Keyring) or KWallet, make it the default, then save again.
var_undefined: {name} is not defined, neither in the workspace nor in the system environment
var_secret: {name} looks like a secret: passwords stay in the keychain, not in variables
var_field_hint: You can write {example}: the value comes from the workspace or the environment.
org_space_vars_hint: Values for connection fields written as {example}. They apply while this workspace is active and win over the system environment. No passwords: those stay in the keychain.
org_space_var_bad_name: Letters, digits and _, not starting with a digit
org_space_var_secret: Looks like a password: keep it in the keychain
form_proxy_user_hint: Empty if the proxy needs no login
proxy_hint: The proxy carries the first leg: to the database, or to the first SSH host.
ssh_jumps_hint: In order: NiceDB enters the first host, from there the next, up to the SSH host. Every host key is verified.
cert_hint: An encrypted key must be PKCS#8 (openssl pkcs8 -topk8); the passphrase stays in the keychain.
deps_empty: The server knows no objects tied to {name}.
deps_from_text: Views read by the engine where it can; routines, macros and trigger bodies from the text of their definitions, where a name quoted in a comment or a string counts as a use.
dz_unsupported: The table designer is not available for this engine yet: write the CREATE TABLE in the editor.
dz_pk_where: Pick the primary key with the key beside the columns.
dz_identity_none: {engine} has no auto-numbered columns: use a sequence as the default.
dz_reorder_hint: {engine} cannot move existing columns: new ones go at the end.
dz_no_indexes: No indexes besides the primary key.
dz_nothing: No changes: the script writes itself as you change the table.
dz_blocked_trigger: No script while the trigger above uses what the change takes away.
dz_blocked: Fill in the flagged fields to see the script.
dz_apply_dry_hint: «Apply» runs the script in a transaction: check the result, then confirm or roll back.
dz_apply_direct_hint: {engine} commits each statement as it runs: «Apply» cannot try it first.
dz_trial: Script run as a trial. Nothing is final until you confirm.
dz_rolled_back: Changes rolled back: the table is as it was.
dz_loading: Reading the structure from the server…
dz_apply_title: Runs the script, with the connection's confirmations
dz_apply_dry_title: Runs the script in a transaction to confirm
dz_reset_hint: Back to the table as the server has it
dz_bad_columns: At least one column is needed.
dz_bad_primary_key: The primary key names a column that does not exist.
dz_bad_index: An index has no name or columns.
dz_bad_foreign_key: A foreign key has no columns or referenced table.
dz_bad_named: To fix: {name} (repeated name, missing type or incomplete columns).
dz_note_drops: Column {name} is dropped with its data.
dz_note_rebuild: {engine} cannot change this in place: the table is created anew and its rows copied.
dz_note_reorder_rewrites: Moving {name} rewrites the whole table: slow on large tables.
dz_note_reorder_unsupported: {engine} cannot reorder columns: the server's order stays.
dz_note_default_constraint: The default constraint {name} is dropped and added again.
dz_note_identity: {engine} cannot turn automatic numbering on or off for {name}: the column must be recreated.
dz_note_comment: {engine} has no comments on tables and columns: they are not saved.
dz_note_not_null: {name} is NOT NULL without a default: it fails if the table already has rows.
dz_note_type: The values of {name} are converted: if one does not fit the new type, the script stops.
dz_note_pk_required: {engine} always needs a primary key: it cannot be removed.
dz_note_trigger: Trigger {name} is created again after the rows are copied.
dz_note_trigger_blocks: Trigger {name} uses {what}, which this change takes away: the table cannot be rebuilt. Change or drop the trigger, then try again.
dz_note_fk_action: {engine} has no cascading actions: {name} is written without them.
chart_need_y: Pick a numeric column for Y, or the count.
chart_need_x: A scatter chart needs a numeric or date X.
chart_skipped_one: 1 row without X was left out.
chart_skipped_other: {count} rows without X were left out.
chart_dropped: Drawn the first {count} categories: aggregate or reduce the categories to see them all.
chart_keys: Arrows move through the points, Home and End jump to the first and last.
gen_lead: Made-up but believable rows, in Italian or English, within the table's constraints. Same seed, same rows.
gen_preview_hint: The first rows, as they will be written.
gen_preview_none: No column to write: the server fills them all.
gen_waiting: {tables}: no rows yet, the links fill in when writing.
gen_cancelled: Cancelled: the transaction was rolled back, no rows written.
gen_rolled_back: Everything rolled back, no rows written.
gen_kept: ClickHouse does not roll back: {rows} rows already written stay.
gen_stopped_kept: Stopped: {rows} rows already written stay, ClickHouse does not roll back.
gen_batches: ClickHouse has no transactions: rows go in batches of 1000. If the server refuses a batch the run stops, and the batches already written stay.
gen_prod_body: Test data is written only on local, development, test or staging connections. Here it would sit next to real data, and a ROLLBACK does not give back the numbers sequences already handed out.
gen_prod_how: To try it, connect a copy of the database as a non-production connection.
gen_confirm_note: All in one transaction: the first error rolls everything back.
gen_p_values: values, comma separated, weight with *: new*3, closed
gen_fault_empty_parent: {table} has no rows: turn on «Parent tables first» or fill it first.
gen_fault_no_unique: Ran out of new values for {columns}: widen the range or ask for fewer rows.
gen_fault_batch: Rows {from}–{to} of {table} refused by the server: {message}
tool_fault_production: Production connection: test data is not written here.
json_expected_value: A value is missing here: quoted text, a number, true, false, null, an object or a list.
json_expected_key: A quoted field name belongs here.
json_expected_colon: A colon belongs after the field name.
json_expected_comma: A comma or a closing bracket is missing.
json_unclosed_string: The quoted text is never closed.
json_trailing: There is more text after the command ends.
json_not_object: A command is a JSON object in braces that starts with its name, such as find or aggregate.
mongo_srv_hint: The host is the cluster name: servers and port come from DNS. The SSH tunnel and the proxy are not used.
doc_not_json: The document is not valid JSON. {problem}
doc_readonly_note: Only the results of a find without a projection can be edited.
sort_not_supported: This engine does not reorder results on the server: change the command's sort.
doc_not_object: A document is a JSON object in braces.
gen_p_weights: A number after * makes a value more frequent: open*3, paid means three open for every paid one.
gen_p_pattern_help: # a digit, ? a letter, * either, {counter} the row number, {year} the year, {column} a value of the row.
gen_p_expr_help: Numeric columns of the row with + − * / %, parentheses, round, min, max, abs.
gen_profile_other: From other tables, by column name
pal_ask_value_hint: Type the value and press Enter.
kv_gone: The key is gone: it expired or someone else removed it.
kv_load_all_hint: Scans on to the end, at most {cap} keys
kv_pick: Pick a key on the left
kv_stream_hint: One field per line: status shipped
kv_truncated: Only the first MB is shown
kv_ttl_bad: Not a valid expiry: for example 90, 15m, 2h, 7d
kv_unknown_type: Type {kind} is not shown here: read it from the command editor.
srv_no_access: The server does not show this to this user.
cluster_items_note: DynamoDB's count, about every six hours
risk_full_scan: KEYS reads every key and holds the server until it is done
clickhouse_http_hint: NiceDB talks to ClickHouse's HTTP interface: 8123 in the clear, 8443 with TLS. The native port 9000 is not used.
cql_form_hint: Also for ScyllaDB. Several nodes separated by commas, all on the same port. With a single node NiceDB always goes through it, even when the cluster announces others. The consistency can also be changed from the editor with CONSISTENCY QUORUM.
es_form_hint: Also for OpenSearch. Empty shows every index; with “orders*, customers” the tree shows only those. With an empty user the password is the encoded API key; with neither, a cluster without security.
ddb_endpoint_hint: Empty uses the region's endpoint; for DynamoDB Local, http://127.0.0.1:8000.
ddb_credentials_hint: With a profile NiceDB reads ~/.aws/credentials; without one it uses the key written here, with the secret in the keychain.
data_ro_engine: Read only: {engine} does not change rows one at a time.
data_ro_engine_hint: To change data, write INSERT, ALTER TABLE … UPDATE or ALTER TABLE … DELETE in the editor: they go through the same production gate.
redis_mode_cluster_hint: Host and port of any node: NiceDB reads the slot map and talks to every master. A cluster has database 0 only.
redis_mode_sentinel_hint: Host and port of a Sentinel; more after a comma (s1:26379, s2:26379). NiceDB asks where the master is and connects to it.
tool_principal_login: A user who signs in (otherwise a role)
tool_mongo_password_hint: Type the password into "pwd" in the command below before you run it: history and the audit log keep it as ••••.
tool_mongo_roles_hint: In MongoDB a user's rights are roles, each on one database; a custom role can hold actions on single collections.
tool_clickhouse_user_hint: The new user cannot sign in yet (HOST NONE): give it a password and hosts from the editor, with ALTER USER … IDENTIFIED BY … HOST ANY.
plan_f_docs_title: {table}: the index lets it read too much ({factor}×)
plan_f_docs_body: With the index {index} the server reads {rows} documents of {table} to return {kept}: the filter on {column} comes after. A compound index that includes {column} makes it read far less.
plan_f_memsort_body: The server sorts {rows} documents of {table} in memory ({size}), because no index gives that order already. An index ending with the sort fields avoids it.
plan_f_memsort_body_nosize: The server sorts {rows} documents of {table} in memory, because no index gives that order already. An index ending with the sort fields avoids it.
dz_note_partial: Index {name}: {engine} has no partial indexes, so the condition is left out.
dz_note_rename_temp: {name} goes through a temporary name, because its new name still belongs to another column.
org_import_done_extras: Added {params} parameter values, {profiles} test data profiles and {marks} pins and bookmarks.
chart_log_stacked: Stacked bars keep a linear scale
chart_log_hidden: {count} values at zero or below stay off the log scale.
chart_cmd_stacked: Chart: stacked or side by side bars
upd_check_hint: At most once a day. NiceDB only downloads the latest.json file of the newest release: no account, no data sent.
upd_ready: Installed: NiceDB reopens on the new version.
upd_saved: This copy cannot replace itself. The verified file is here: {path}
upd_trust: Every update is signed: NiceDB installs it only if the signature matches the key built into the app.
upd_err_signature: The update's signature is not valid: it was not installed.
upd_err_none: No update to install: check again.
upd_err_install: Update not installed, NiceDB is unchanged ({detail}).
upd_err_restart: Restart failed: open NiceDB again by hand ({detail}).
about_desc: A client for SQL, document and key-value databases. Open source under the GPL, version 3 or later.
about_third_hint: {count} components shipped in the app: Rust and JavaScript libraries, fonts, sounds and icons.
about_none: No component with this name or licence.
about_load_failed: The licences did not load: the app was updated while this page was open. Reload the page to see them.
about_standard: The package ships no licence text: the standard text is shown below.
flavor_hint_timescale: PostgreSQL with the TimescaleDB extension. Hypertables, chunks, continuous aggregates and compression show in the tree and in Tools › Space.
flavor_hint_yugabyte: YSQL, YugabyteDB's Postgres side, on port 5433. The catalog is Postgres 11's and locks are distributed.
flavor_hint_neon: Copy the URL from Neon's console. With -pooler in the host you go through the pooler: session settings do not outlive the transaction.
flavor_hint_supabase: db.<project>.supabase.co is the direct connection. Through the pooler, port 6543 works per transaction, 5432 per session.
flavor_hint_tidb: MySQL protocol on port 4000. Plans, monitoring and lock waits come from TiDB's own tables.
flavor_hint_planetscale: Each password works for one branch only. On the production branch the schema changes through deploy requests.
form_url_paste_hint: Paste a URL: host, port, database and user fill in, the password goes to the keychain.
form_url_bad: Not a PostgreSQL or MySQL URL that can be read.
tls_required_note: The service only accepts encrypted connections.
tag_cagg_tip: Continuous aggregate: refreshed from its hypertable
limit_pooled_session: Through the pooler, SET, temporary tables, advisory locks and LISTEN last only inside the transaction.
limit_scale_to_zero: The compute stops when idle: the first query after a pause waits for it to start.
limit_managed_schemas: auth, storage and the other platform schemas belong to Supabase: changing them can break the project.
limit_foreign_keys_optional: Foreign keys are enforced only if the database has them turned on.
limit_deploy_requests: On the production branch the schema changes through a deploy request, not direct DDL.
limit_no_routines: Procedures, triggers and events do not go through Vitess.
limit_distributed_locks: Locks are distributed: monitoring sees the waits, not the whole tree.
limit_own_dump_tool: Backup uses the standard tool; the engine's own features need its own dump tool.
limit_hypertable_dump: pg_dump saves hypertables, but restoring needs TimescaleDB's procedures.
limit_dashboard_users: Users and grants are managed in the service's dashboard.
limit_own_plans: Plans come from TiDB's EXPLAIN: operators and tasks read differently from MySQL.
ddb_b_hint: A Scan or Query built from the fields; below, the call that goes into the editor.
ddb_b_limit_hint: With a limit DynamoDB reads a single page of at most that many items, and filters afterwards.
ddb_b_pages_hint: Without a limit NiceDB follows the pages up to the connection's row limit.
cmp_outside_path: {name} is not on the search_path: it lives in {schema}
vp_hex_hint: Two digits per byte; spaces and line breaks are ignored.
vp_hex_invalid: These are not whole bytes of hex: use pairs of digits 0-9 and a-f.
vp_hex_too_big: Over 1 MB the bytes are not edited by hand: load a file.
chq_no_quotas: No quota for this user or role.
chq_no_profiles: No settings profile for this user or role.
chq_no_policies: No row policy for this user or role.
chq_drop_note: Whoever used it loses its limits or settings at once.
chq_note: Quotas, profiles and policies are written in SQL: NiceDB drafts the statement, you can edit it, and it runs as from the editor, with the production check and the log.
sentinel_tip: The master the Sentinels point to now. When they move it, NiceDB reconnects to the new one by itself.
sentinel_failover: The Sentinels moved master {name} from {from} to {to}: NiceDB now works on the new one.
ora_connect_string_hint: host:port/service, or a whole (DESCRIPTION=…) descriptor. No SSH tunnel or proxy.
ora_sid_check: The name is a SID, not a service
fb_no_tls_hint: Firebird has no TLS setting: Firebird encrypts the protocol itself (wire crypt), as the server’s WireCrypt setting says.
ora_tls_hint: With TLS NiceDB speaks TCPS (usually port 2484). The CA file becomes the only trusted root; “Encrypted, unverified” skips only the name check, the certificate chain is still verified.
tool_backup_unsupported_oracle: Oracle is not copied from here: use Data Pump (expdp and impdp) or RMAN on the server.
run_cancel_none: This engine's driver cannot interrupt the running query: the script stops once it finishes.
run_cancel_fetches: Stops the rows at the next batch. Work the server has started goes on: stopping it needs the ALTER SYSTEM privilege.
plan_reason_no_privilege: For real timings Oracle needs SELECT on V$SESSION, V$SQL and V$SQL_PLAN_STATISTICS_ALL (SELECT_CATALOG_ROLE, for instance): this is the EXPLAIN PLAN estimate.
snip_block_desc: Anonymous block with one variable, closed by /
plan_measured_rolled_back_oracle: DISPLAY_CURSOR · run at {time} in a rolled-back transaction
eng_locked: A saved connection can only switch to products of the same engine
agg_widen_tip: Compute on the server, over every row of the result
agg_widen_failed: The server could not compute the totals: {message}
chart_partial_none: Chart of the {count} loaded rows. With an aggregation every row is grouped on the server.
chart_full_on: All rows, grouped on the server.
chart_full_failed: The server could not group the rows: {message}
pal_cmd_tab_close_right: Close the tabs to the right
pal_cmd_export_result: Export the result to a file…
gen_fault_check: No generated row satisfies the check {expr} after 200 tries. Change the values of the columns it uses.
gen_rule_column_tip: Read as the allowed values or range of one column: generated values already fit.
gen_rule_row_tip: Each generated row is tested against the check; a row that breaks it is made again.
gen_rule_server_tip: It uses functions or subqueries NiceDB does not evaluate: the server checks it, and a value that breaks it rolls the insert back.
grid_edit_huge_tip: The value is too large for a field: type to replace it, Esc to leave it as it is. The Value panel shows it whole.
settings_drivers_hint: Some databases need their vendor's client, which NiceDB cannot ship. Tell it here where you put it.
settings_db2_hint: The clidriver folder unpacked from IBM's archive (odbc_cli, free, no account needed). On Windows, first run clidriver\bin\db2cli install -setup as administrator. It applies to connections opened from now on.
hana_form_hint: For a multitenant system, give the tenant's SQL port and its name; for a single database, leave the tenant empty. This engine has not been tried on a real server yet.
db2_form_hint: It needs IBM's CLI driver: download it from IBM and choose its folder in Settings › Drivers.
odbc_driver_hint: A data source already set up, or the path of the driver library or its registered name.
odbc_hint: The driver's keywords, separated by semicolons. User and password reach the driver as UID and PWD; the password is kept in the keychain.
dz_note_rename_table: Table {name} keeps its name: {engine} cannot rename tables.
conn_downgrade_title: Take this connection out of production?
conn_downgrade_note: Writes will no longer ask for an unlock or a confirmation, and the server will no longer be read-only. The change is kept in the write log.
prefs_loosen_line: It applies to every production connection, including the ones already open.
prefs_loosen_note: Writes will ask for fewer unlocks or confirmations. The change is kept in the write log.
kv_entries_keys: Arrow keys pick an item, Shift+F10 opens its menu.
kv_entries_keys_edit: Arrow keys pick an item, Enter edits it, Delete removes it, Shift+F10 opens its menu.
settings_pointers_hint: Arrow, text cursor and handles drawn in the shape and colours of the style. With high contrast or forced colours on, the system ones stay.
pointers_offer_body: From this version NiceDB can draw the mouse pointer in the shape and colours of the style you use. Turn it on?
pointers_offer_later: You can change it any time in Settings › Appearance.
